t.E529.agn: In 1965, JECFA set the ADI for calcium oxide as 'not limited'; the evaluation stated that no toxicological reason was seen to limit use in line with good manufacturing practice, but that the total calcium intake from these additives should be kept in mind from a nutritional point of view. In the EU it is a Group I additive; EFSA's re-evaluation has not yet been published (it was included in a call for data in 2016).
t.E529.found.0: May be used at quantum satis (as much as needed) in many foods in the EU
t.E529.prod: It is obtained by burning (calcining) limestone or magnesium minerals.
t.E529.regx.1: Group I additive; generally permitted at quantum satis (as much as needed).
t.E529.regx.2: Included in the call for use/concentration data as part of the re-evaluation (deadline 31.01.2017).
t.E529.summary: Calcium oxide (quicklime). Used as an acidity regulator and flour treatment agent.
t.E529.what: It is a base (quicklime) used to regulate acidity and to neutralise; it is also used as a dough conditioner. It reacts with water to form calcium hydroxide and with acids to form calcium salts.
